w: Thessaloniki's archaeological museum tracks Macedonia's story from Prehistoric flints through Archaic, Classical, Hellenistic and Roman finds, most excavated right here in the city but drawn from across the wider region too - a full timeline of the north Aegean's ancient life under one roof.
s: Macedonia's ancient story, one gallery at a time
_facts: Holds and interprets artifacts from Prehistoric, Archaic, Classical, Hellenistic and Roman periods
Mostly from the city of Thessaloniki but also from the wider Macedonia region

w: Thessaloniki's grand civic square opens straight onto the waterfront, laid out in 1918 by French architect Ernest Hébrard though most of what stands today went up in the 1950s. The twelve buildings ringing it have been listed since 1950, restored again in the 2000s - a well-photographed piece of city planning.
_facts: Main city square on Nikis avenue on the waterfront, designed by Ernest Hébrard in 1918
Most of the square was built in the 1950s; the 12 surrounding buildings listed since 1950, restored in the 2000s

w: An 11th-century Byzantine church whose mosaics are reason enough to duck inside - one of fifteen Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments on Thessaloniki's UNESCO listing. The Ottomans turned it into a mosque in the 15th century; it was reconsecrated as a church again in the 20th, swinging back after five hundred years.
_facts: 11th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church, one of 15 UNESCO-listed Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments of Thessaloniki
Converted to a mosque in the 15th century Ottoman era, reconsecrated as a church in the 20th century

w: Built in 1460 as an Ottoman mosque, abandoned by the 1820s, then reborn for decades as a cinema - most Thessalonians still call it 'Alkazar' after the picture house rather than its original name. A five-century building with two entirely different lives stacked inside it.
s: Ottoman mosque turned cinema, still called Alkazar
_facts: Built 1460 as an Ottoman mosque, abandoned in the 1820s
Modern Thessalonians commonly know it as Alkazar, after a cinema that operated on the premises for decades

w: Housed in a 1900s building by architect Vitaliano Poselli, Thessaloniki's War Museum walks visitors from the Balkan Wars through the Asia Minor Campaign to the 1944 liberation from German occupation. Uniforms, weapons and wartime photographs keep Northern Greece's military memory alive.
s: A century of Northern Greece's wars, under one roof
_facts: Opened October 2000, housed in a building by architect Vitaliano Poselli built 1900-1902
Covers the Balkan Wars, WWI, the Asia Minor Campaign, and the liberation from German occupation in WWII

w: Greece's first black-and-white television broadcast beamed out from this 76-metre concrete tower in 1971, and it later carried the antennas for an experimental 1970s mobile phone network. Today a revolving restaurant turns slowly on top, open year-round, while the tower doubles as a modern monument of the skyline.
s: Where Greek TV was born, now a revolving restaurant
_facts: 76-metre tower at the Thessaloniki International Exhibition Center, opened 1970, first Greek TV broadcasts from it in 1971
Used in the 1970s for an experimental VHF mobile telephone network; a revolving restaurant now operates year-round on top

w: Known in Judaeo-Spanish as the Kal de los Monastirlis, this Orthodox synagogue is one of the last physical traces of Thessaloniki's once-vibrant Sephardic Jewish community - a congregation that shaped the city for centuries before the Holocaust all but erased it.
s: A last trace of Thessaloniki's Sephardic community
_facts: Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, known in Judaeo-Spanish as Kal de los Monastirlis
Part of the once-vibrant Jewish community of Thessaloniki

w: Thessaloniki's contemporary art museum spent decades going by a different name - the Macedonian Museum of Contemporary Art - before rebranding into the MOMus network on the Thessaloniki International Fair grounds. Modern and contemporary Greek work gets a home among the city's older, more classical collections.
s: Contemporary Greek art on the old Fair grounds
_facts: Contemporary art museum in the Thessaloniki International Fair area, formerly known as the Macedonian Museum of Contemporary Art

w: More than a thousand works live inside Villa Bianca, an eclectic mansion on Vassilissis Olgas Avenue that the city's art gallery has called home since 2013. The collection runs from centuries-old icons to modern Greek painting - past exhibitions have brought in Max Ernst himself.
s: A thousand works inside an eclectic-style villa
_facts: Founded 1966, over 1,000 works, housed in Villa Bianca on Vassilissis Olgas Avenue since 2013
Collections include Byzantine and post-Byzantine icons spanning six centuries and Modern Greek art; has hosted Max Ernst exhibitions
